A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, method, and principal experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original inpainting, super-resolution, style-guided and mask-guided generation results, together with empirical Jacobian analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original generation experiments and adds caption-assisted super-resolution, MNIST update comparisons, finite-difference ablations, and rectified-flow examples.

M1.justification: The central finite-difference Jacobian-vector sampler is retained. v3 adds an optional encoder-Jacobian approximation that avoids decoder backpropagation (A.4) and line-search step selection for InstaFlow (B.4). Algorithm 1 also revises the update sign and DDIM noise coefficient; these written corrections do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: v3 adds MNIST training and single-pixel digit-editing experiments in A.3. ImageNet, WikiArt/PartiPrompts, FFHQ, and the earlier synthetic-image scenarios remain. Captioning and distilled-model experiments modify configurations within retained image-reconstruction tasks.

E2.justification: The principal benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged; P2L becomes explicitly labeled 'P2L + captions.' v3 adds exact/pseudoinverse Newton updates to the update-direction comparison in A.3 and exact Jacobian-vector computation as a reference for finite differences in A.5.

E3.justification: Added experimental designs include Qwen-generated conditioning captions, a 25M-parameter model trained on 32×32 MNIST images and tested at t=500/700, a finite-difference step-size sweep, and five-step InstaFlow sampling with an Euler solver and line search. These substantially extend the evaluated configurations; the main retained benchmark splits and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially strengthens direct testing of the approximation through exact-Newton comparisons, finite-difference versus exact-JVP controls, step-size sensitivity, and encoder-based versus decoder-backpropagation comparisons. It also tests caption conditioning and distilled-model failure behavior. Earlier convergence, Jacobian-asymmetry, and optimization-step analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 in v3 newly states that experiments were performed once and explicitly acknowledges the absence of error bars. This discloses run information without establishing a change in run counts. Both versions retain multiple-seed toy illustrations and provide no benchmark confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Most original benchmark scores remain unchanged. New results include captioned super-resolution at PSNR 24.95, LPIPS 0.405, and FID 44.74 (v3 Table 2), Table 6 ablations, and MNIST/VAE/rectified-flow comparisons. These are additional settings, not improvements to unchanged uncaptioned results. FreeDoM's style score changes from 498.8 to 498.08; ablation runtimes and absolute memory measurements are added, while mask-generation runtimes are removed.

T1.justification: v3 adds the encoder/decoder Jacobian derivation in A.4 and corrects finite-difference sign inconsistencies. Most convergence mathematics is retained from v2 Appendix A.1 and moved into Section 3. The new assertion that a bounded Jacobian spectrum permits a convergent learning rate is stronger than the stated norm condition alone supports.

C1.justification: Both versions claim fast, training-free constrained sampling with competitive generation quality and inexpensive denoiser forward passes. Newton approximation becomes more prominent in the abstract and conclusion, but this interpretation and the principal efficiency and applicability claims already appear in v2.

C2.justification: v3 adds concrete limitations for high classifier-free guidance and distilled models, explains their optimization difficulties, and attributes P2L's advantage more specifically to text conditioning. It also discusses the encoder variant's computational tradeoff. Conversely, Table 4 newly claims no compromise in prompt faithfulness despite retaining lower CLIP scores than the competing guided methods.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the default finite-difference step size, PyTorch's double-backward JVP implementation, MNIST architecture and padding, and the Qwen caption source. It reports absolute memory requirements and DDIM/PNDM implementation availability. The repository and face-parser links already exist in v2; gradient normalization was also previously documented in its appendix.

R1.justification: v3 adds references concerning numerical optimization, captioning models, alternative diffusion solvers, and distilled models. It credits Sorrenson et al. for encoder/decoder Jacobian inversion and claims a new application to diffusion autoencoders. The central positioning against existing constrained-sampling methods remains intact.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method narrative are extensively rewritten around Newton approximation. Convergence reasoning moves into Section 3, symmetry experiments move into Appendix A.2, nonlinear tasks are grouped together, and the appendices are reorganized. A limitations paragraph and conference checklist are added.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from two-column to single-column layout, with extensive figure relocation and rearrangement. The original combined reconstruction table is split, box-inpainting ablations are merged into the main comparison, and new Table 6 and Figures 11, 12, and 16 are added. v3 Figure 2 redisplays part of the earlier Jacobian visualization.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the exact-Newton and exact-JVP controls more directly test the central approximation, while caption-conditioned evaluation and concrete failure conditions improve interpretation and practical guidance. These provide a net quality gain. The gain is tempered by the unsupported bounded-spectrum assurance in Section 3 and Table 4's stronger prompt-faithfulness claim despite unchanged, lower CLIP scores.
